subject: Police charge crowds at Brussels student march
posts:
Riot police deploy water cannons and tear gas against thousands of students marching in Brussels against tuition hikes and cuts.
Evidence: Student march, Police intervention, Dispersal via force.
#Aletheia #Brussels

Thousands of students and teachers marched peacefully in Brussels to protest higher tuition fees, sweeping education reforms, and funding cuts.

Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.7) — Exclusive Constraint

- Belgian Police: FAIL (-0.8, -0.7) — Deployed tear gas and water cannons.
Thousands of demonstrators flooded Brussels streets to protest austerity measures and tuition hikes affecting higher education institutions across Belgium.

The Poison:
State authorities chose physical suppression over dialogue, criminalizing legitimate grievances regarding educational access.
Plane Error: Confusing civic expression (WHO) with public disorder (HOW). State power frames legitimate protests as security threats to justify force.

Social Physics Analysis:
Authorities ran a Smart Selfish Maneuver, framing student demonstrators as security risks to justify disproportionate force and suppress dissent.

Promising inclusive education while deploying riot police inverts civic trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: Peaceful protests against austerity were met with aggressive police crowd control.
The Unavoidable Lie: State force was a proportionate response to public safety.
